description.summary: outputs that exist only to be captured

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a privileged client create outputs that have no physical display behind them: a tablet used as a second monitor, a headless remote desktop, a stream of an extra workspace. To the rest of the session a virtual output is an ordinary output. It has a wl_output global, windows can be placed and fullscreened on it, layer surfaces can anchor to it, and output management lists and configures it like any other head.
What a virtual output lacks is a display to pace it. Its frame clock is driven by the client instead: the compositor renders a virtual output, and sends frame callbacks to the surfaces on it, only when the client asks with request_frame. A client streaming the output to an encoder asks once per encoded frame, so the applications on the output draw exactly as often as their pixels are consumed. The pixels themselves are obtained with crownos-screencast-v1, by capturing the virtual output's wl_output.
Only privileged clients can bind the manager global. A compositor must not expose it to sandboxed clients.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_virtual_output_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_virtual_output_v1 objects.

entry.name: invalid_name
entry.summary: the name is empty, too long or contains a disallowed character

entry.name: invalid_mode
entry.summary: the size, refresh rate or scale is out of range

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Virtual outputs created through it are unaffected and exist until they are destroyed individually.

request.name: create_output
request.description:
Create a virtual output. The compositor answers with either created, once the output's wl_output global has been announced, or closed.
name identifies the output to the user and to output management. It must be 1 to 32 characters from [A-Za-z0-9_-]; anything else raises invalid_name. The compositor namespaces it, so the wl_output and output-management head of the new output are not called name itself but whatever the created event reports. Creating a second output with a name already in use is not an error: the second output is closed with name_taken.
width and height are the output's mode in pixels, both between 1 and 16384. refresh_mhz is the nominal refresh rate in millihertz that the output advertises in its mode; since the frame clock is driven by request_frame it is informational, but clients use it to pick animation rates, so it should match the rate the client intends to request frames at. It must be non-zero. scale_120 is the output scale in 120ths (120 is scale 1, 180 is 1.5), between 60 and 480. Any value out of range raises invalid_mode.

interface.name: crownos_virtual_output_v1
interface.description:
A virtual output, owned by the client that created it. It exists from the created event until the object is destroyed or closed is sent.
Requests other than destroy are ignored before created and after closed, since the client cannot tell exactly when either happens.

entry.name: invalid_mode
entry.summary: set_mode was given a size, refresh rate or scale out of range

entry.name: name_taken
entry.summary: another output already uses this name

entry.name: revoked
entry.summary: the compositor or the user removed the output

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: the compositor could not create the output

request.name: destroy
request.description: Remove the virtual output. Its wl_output global is removed and windows on it move to another output, exactly as when a monitor is unplugged.

request.name: set_mode
request.description: Change the size, nominal refresh rate and scale of the output, with the same ranges as create_output; a value out of range raises invalid_mode. Clients on the output see an ordinary mode change, and screencast sessions capturing it receive new constraints.

request.name: request_frame

description.summary: advance the output's frame clock by one frame

request.description:
Tell the compositor that the consumer is ready for another frame.
In response the compositor advances the output by one frame: it renders the output for every screencast session capturing it (subject to that session's own damage and slot rules, so an unchanged output still produces no new frame), and sends frame callbacks and presentation feedback to the surfaces shown on it.
Nothing on a virtual output is rendered, and no surface on it receives frame callbacks, between two request_frame requests. Several requests before the compositor gets round to the frame collapse into one.

event.name: created
event.description:
The output was created and its wl_output global announced. name is the output's full name: the name the wl_output name event (version 4 and later) reports, and the head name output management uses. A client binds the wl_output whose name event matches it.
Sent at most once. created and closed are mutually exclusive as a first event, but closed may follow created.

event.name: closed
event.description: The output was removed, or could never be created. The object is inert from here on and should be destroyed. This is the last event sent on the object.
